messages.content: [MD-4121] Our app only gets SD renditions on the lumen-l3, while the atlas-a1 gets HD. Same account. Why?

input.query: Widevine security level L1 L3 HD

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel")`.
- A device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or a failed keybox
  provisioning; the license server then refuses HD keys.
- Log the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal apart from a
  network or provisioning error."}, {"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.
- Too many codec instances are alive at once. Hardware codecs are a shared, limited resource;
  release codecs you no longer use.
- The output `Surface` was released while the codec still used it.

Log the `diagnosticInfo` string from the exception; it names the failing component."}]}

messages.content: [MD-4124] progressive_late_moov.mp4 takes about 10 seconds to start over HTTP but plays fine afterwards. Why?

input.query: moov atom position progressive playback startup

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "mp4-faststart", "title": "Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)", "text": "# Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)

An MP4 file's index (the `moov` atom) is often written at the end of the file by recorders and
encoders. A progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can
begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests.

Checks and fix:
- `ffprobe -v trace file.mp4 2>&1 | grep -m2 -E "type:'(moov|mdat)'"` shows which atom comes first.
- Remux with the index at the front: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart out.mp4`.
- For adaptive streaming, prefer fragmented MP4 (DASH or HLS) instead."}, {"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel")`.
- A device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or a failed keybox
  provisioning; the license server then refuses HD keys.
- Log the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal apart from a
  network or provisioning error."}]}

messages.content: [MD-4130] Before offering HDR renditions, how should the app check the display?

input.query: Display HDR10 capability API

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

Checks:
- Ask the display what it supports: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` (or `Display.isHdr()` on API 26+).
- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason
  HDR output gets flattened.
- Confirm the decoder output format reports the expected colour transfer
  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.
- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or
  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}, {"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}, {"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}]}

messages.content: [MD-4139] On the atlas-a1, HDR (hdr10_hevc_1080p.mp4) looks grey only inside our app. Ideas?

input.query: HDR looks grey washed out in app

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

Checks:
- Ask the display what it supports: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` (or `Display.isHdr()` on API 26+).
- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason
  HDR output gets flattened.
- Confirm the decoder output format reports the expected colour transfer
  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.
- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or
  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}, {"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}]}

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.

  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}]}

input.query: HDR colour flat player vs gallery surface colour mode

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

Checks:
- Ask the display what it supports: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` (or `Display.isHdr()` on API 26+).
- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason
  HDR output gets flattened.
- Confirm the decoder output format reports the expected colour transfer
  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.
- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or
  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}, {"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}]}

messages.content: [MD-4115] Can we rely on AV1 on Android? Which version added a decoder and how do we detect hardware?

input.query: AV1 hardware decoder Android version detect hardware

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.
- Too many codec instances are alive at once. Hardware codecs are a shared, limited resource;
  release codecs you no longer use.
- The output `Surface` was released while the codec still used it.

Log the `diagnosticInfo` string from the exception; it names the failing component."}]}

messages.content: [MD-4120] MediaCodec.configure() throws for our 10-bit HEVC stream on the lumen-l3. Why?

input.query: 10-bit HEVC Main10 decoder profile configure

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.
- Too many codec instances are alive at once. Hardware codecs are a shared, limited resource;
  release codecs you no longer use.
- The output `Surface` was released while the codec still used it.

Log the `diagnosticInfo` string from the exception; it names the failing component."}, {"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}]}

messages.content: [MD-4143] Our podcast app keeps playing during phone calls. How do we fix it?

input.query: audio focus pause playback during phone calls

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}, {"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel")`.
- A device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or a failed keybox
  provisioning; the license server then refuses HD keys.
- Log the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal apart from a
  network or provisioning error."}]}

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.

Checks:

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

Checks:
- Ask the display what it supports: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` (or `Display.isHdr()` on API 26+).
- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason
  HDR output gets flattened.
- Confirm the decoder output format reports the expected colour transfer
  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.
- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or
  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}, {"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.

messages.content: [MD-4149] Will the atlas-a1 decode av1_2160p60.mkv in hardware?

input.query: AV1 hardware decoder 4K60

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.
- Too many codec instances are alive at once. Hardware codecs are a shared, limited resource;
  release codecs you no longer use.
- The output `Surface` was released while the codec still used it.

Log the `diagnosticInfo` string from the exception; it names the failing component."}]}

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason
  HDR output gets flattened.

  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.
- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or
  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}, {"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:

messages.content: [MD-4192] Startup for progressive_late_moov.mp4 is slow on mobile networks; seeking later is fine. Cause?

input.query: moov atom position progressive playback startup

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "mp4-faststart", "title": "Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)", "text": "# Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)

An MP4 file's index (the `moov` atom) is often written at the end of the file by recorders and
encoders. A progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can
begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests.

Checks and fix:
- `ffprobe -v trace file.mp4 2>&1 | grep -m2 -E "type:'(moov|mdat)'"` shows which atom comes first.
- Remux with the index at the front: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart out.mp4`.
- For adaptive streaming, prefer fragmented MP4 (DASH or HLS) instead."}, {"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel")`.
- A device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or a failed keybox
  provisioning; the license server then refuses HD keys.
- Log the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal apart from a
  network or provisioning error."}]}

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`

Log the `diagnosticInfo` string from the exception; it names the failing component."}, {"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}]}

messages.content: [MD-4103] progressive_late_moov.mp4 takes about 10 seconds to start over HTTP but plays fine afterwards. Why?

input.query: progressive playback moov mdat faststart

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "mp4-faststart", "title": "Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)", "text": "# Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)

An MP4 file's index (the `moov` atom) is often written at the end of the file by recorders and
encoders. A progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can
begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests.

Checks and fix:
- `ffprobe -v trace file.mp4 2>&1 | grep -m2 -E "type:'(moov|mdat)'"` shows which atom comes first.
- Remux with the index at the front: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart out.mp4`.
- For adaptive streaming, prefer fragmented MP4 (DASH or HLS) instead."}, {"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel")`.
- A device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or a failed keybox
  provisioning; the license server then refuses HD keys.
- Log the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal apart from a
  network or provisioning error."}]}

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10

devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

Checks:
- Ask the display what it supports: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` (or `Display.isHdr()` on API 26+).
- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason
  HDR output gets flattened.
- Confirm the decoder output format reports the expected colour transfer
  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.
- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or
  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}, {"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "mp4-faststart", "title": "Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)", "text": "# Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)

An MP4 file's index (the `moov` atom) is often written at the end of the file by recorders and
encoders. A progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can
begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests.

Checks and fix:
- `ffprobe -v trace file.mp4 2>&1 | grep -m2 -E "type:'(moov|mdat)'"` shows which atom comes first.
- Remux with the index at the front: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart out.mp4`.
- For adaptive streaming, prefer fragmented MP4 (DASH or HLS) instead."}]}

messages.content: [MD-4187] Premium HD titles fall back to 480p on the lumen-l3 but not the atlas-a1. What's different?

input.query: Widevine security level L1 L3 HD

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel")`.
- A device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or a failed keybox
  provisioning; the license server then refuses HD keys.
- Log the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal apart from a
  network or provisioning error."}, {"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.
- Too many codec instances are alive at once. Hardware codecs are a shared, limited resource;
  release codecs you no longer use.
- The output `Surface` was released while the codec still used it.

Log the `diagnosticInfo` string from the exception; it names the failing component."}]}

messages.content: [MD-4153] Why is DRM content capped at SD on the lumen-l3?

input.query: Widevine L3 DRM capped SD

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel")`.
- A device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or a failed keybox
  provisioning; the license server then refuses HD keys.
- Log the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal apart from a
  network or provisioning error."}]}

messages.content: [MD-4116] Configuring the decoder for HEVC Main 10 fails on lumen-l3 with CodecException. What to do?

input.query: HEVC Main 10 decoder configure CodecException

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.
- Too many codec instances are alive at once. Hardware codecs are a shared, limited resource;
  release codecs you no longer use.
- The output `Surface` was released while the codec still used it.

Log the `diagnosticInfo` string from the exception; it names the failing component."}, {"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

Checks:
- Ask the display what it supports: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` (or `Display.isHdr()` on API 26+).
- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason
  HDR output gets flattened.
- Confirm the decoder output format reports the expected colour transfer
  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.
- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or
  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}]}

messages.content: [MD-4157] av1_2160p60.mkv plays like a slideshow on lumen-l3 test phones. What's the cause?

input.query: AV1 software decoder dropped frames 4K

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

Checks:
- Ask the display what it supports: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` (or `Display.isHdr()` on API 26+).
- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason
  HDR output gets flattened.
- Confirm the decoder output format reports the expected colour transfer
  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.
- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or
  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}]}

messages.content: [MD-4183] Our podcast app keeps playing during phone calls. How do we fix it?

input.query: audio focus phone call pause playback

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}, {"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}]}

messages.content: [MD-4126] Our app only gets SD renditions on the lumen-l3, while the atlas-a1 gets HD. Same account. Why?

input.query: Widevine security level SD HD renditions

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel")`.
- A device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or a failed keybox
  provisioning; the license server then refuses HD keys.
- Log the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal apart from a
  network or provisioning error."}, {"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.
- Too many codec instances are alive at once. Hardware codecs are a shared, limited resource;
  release codecs you no longer use.
- The output `Surface` was released while the codec still used it.

Log the `diagnosticInfo` string from the exception; it names the failing component."}]}

messages.content: [MD-4142] How do we detect at runtime whether the screen can show HDR?

input.query: detect HDR display support at runtime

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

Checks:
- Ask the display what it supports: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` (or `Display.isHdr()` on API 26+).
- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason
  HDR output gets flattened.
- Confirm the decoder output format reports the expected colour transfer
  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.
- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or
  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}, {"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}]}

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.
- Too many codec instances are alive at once. Hardware codecs are a shared, limited resource;
  release codecs you no longer use.
- The output `Surface` was released while the codec still used it.

Log the `diagnosticInfo` string from the exception; it names the failing component."}, {"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}]}

content.content: {"log": "live_resume.txt", "pattern": "error|exception|expired|403|401|token|resume", "matches": 7, "lines": ["L2: 11-21 09:26:40.017  9402  9402 I LivePlayer: onResume: resuming live playback", "L4: 11-21 09:26:40.240  9402  9402 E ExoPlayerImplInternal: Playback error", "L5: 11-21 09:26:40.240  9402  9402 E ExoPlayerImplInternal:   androidx.media3.exoplayer.ExoPlaybackException: Source error", "L6: 11-21 09:26:40.240  9402  9402 E ExoPlayerImplInternal:       at androidx.media3.exoplayer.ExoPlayerImplInternal.handleIoException(ExoPlayerImplInternal.java)", "L7: 11-21 09:26:40.240  9402  9402 E ExoPlayerImplInternal:   Caused by: androidx.media3.exoplayer.source.BehindLiveWindowException", "L8: 11-21 09:26:40.241  9402  9402 E LivePlayer: onPlayerError code=1002 (ERROR_CODE_BEHIND_LIVE_WINDOW)", "L9: 11-21 09:26:40.242  9402  9402 I LivePlayer: showing error screen; no retry configured"]}

{"results": [{"id": "behind-live-window", "title": "BehindLiveWindowException in Media3 / ExoPlayer live streams", "text": "# BehindLiveWindowException in Media3 / ExoPlayer live streams

A live stream exposes a sliding window of segments. If playback falls further behind than
the window (long pause, slow network, app in the background), the segments it needs are gone
and the player raises a `BehindLiveWindowException`, surfaced as a `PlaybackException` with
error code `ERROR_CODE_BEHIND_LIVE_WINDOW`.

Fix: in `Player.Listener.onPlayerError`, check for that error code, then call
`player.seekToDefaultPosition()` followed by `player.prepare()` to rejoin at the live edge.
Consider a longer live window on the server or a smaller target live offset on the client."}, {"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}]}

messages.content: [MD-4144] From which Android version is there an AV1 decoder, and how do we check for hardware support?

input.query: AV1 decoder Android version hardware support detection

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.
- Too many codec instances are alive at once. Hardware codecs are a shared, limited resource;
  release codecs you no longer use.
- The output `Surface` was released while the codec still used it.

Log the `diagnosticInfo` string from the exception; it names the failing component."}, {"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}]}

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel")`.
- A device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or a failed keybox
  provisioning; the license server then refuses HD keys.
- Log the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal apart from a

again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.

messages.content: [MD-4196] Can you confirm progressive_faststart.mp4 is laid out for progressive playback? Startup is slow.

input.query: progressive playback moov mdat faststart

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "mp4-faststart", "title": "Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)", "text": "# Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)

An MP4 file's index (the `moov` atom) is often written at the end of the file by recorders and
encoders. A progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can
begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests.

Checks and fix:
- `ffprobe -v trace file.mp4 2>&1 | grep -m2 -E "type:'(moov|mdat)'"` shows which atom comes first.
- Remux with the index at the front: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart out.mp4`.
- For adaptive streaming, prefer fragmented MP4 (DASH or HLS) instead."}, {"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel")`.
- A device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or a failed keybox
  provisioning; the license server then refuses HD keys.
- Log the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal apart from a
  network or provisioning error."}]}

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.
- Too many codec instances are alive at once. Hardware codecs are a shared, limited resource;
  release codecs you no longer use.
- The output `Surface` was released while the codec still used it.

Log the `diagnosticInfo` string from the exception; it names the failing component."}]}

messages.content: [MD-4177] Is the A/V sync issue in av_offset_300ms.mp4 caused by our player or by the file?

input.query: audio ahead of video A/V sync offset start_time

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}, {"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

Checks:
- Ask the display what it supports: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` (or `Display.isHdr()` on API 26+).
- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason
  HDR output gets flattened.
- Confirm the decoder output format reports the expected colour transfer
  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.
- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or
  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}]}

devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "behind-live-window", "title": "BehindLiveWindowException in Media3 / ExoPlayer live streams", "text": "# BehindLiveWindowException in Media3 / ExoPlayer live streams

A live stream exposes a sliding window of segments. If playback falls further behind than
the window (long pause, slow network, app in the background), the segments it needs are gone
and the player raises a `BehindLiveWindowException`, surfaced as a `PlaybackException` with

messages.content: [MD-4147] Can we rely on AV1 on Android? Which version added a decoder and how do we detect hardware?

input.query: AV1 decoder Android version hardware support detection

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.
- Too many codec instances are alive at once. Hardware codecs are a shared, limited resource;
  release codecs you no longer use.
- The output `Surface` was released while the codec still used it.

Log the `diagnosticInfo` string from the exception; it names the failing component."}, {"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}]}

or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:

  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

messages.content: [MD-4133] Why does progressive_late_moov.mp4 have a long startup delay when streamed progressively?

input.query: progressive playback moov mdat faststart

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "mp4-faststart", "title": "Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)", "text": "# Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)

An MP4 file's index (the `moov` atom) is often written at the end of the file by recorders and
encoders. A progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can
begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests.

Checks and fix:
- `ffprobe -v trace file.mp4 2>&1 | grep -m2 -E "type:'(moov|mdat)'"` shows which atom comes first.
- Remux with the index at the front: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart out.mp4`.
- For adaptive streaming, prefer fragmented MP4 (DASH or HLS) instead."}, {"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel")`.
- A device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or a failed keybox
  provisioning; the license server then refuses HD keys.
- Log the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal apart from a
  network or provisioning error."}]}

messages.content: [MD-4150] QA says the AV1 4K clip av1_2160p60.mkv stutters on the lumen-l3 but not on the atlas-a1. Explain?

input.query: AV1 4K60 decode hardware software

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel")`.
- A device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or a failed keybox
  provisioning; the license server then refuses HD keys.
- Log the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal apart from a
  network or provisioning error."}]}

messages.content: [MD-4131] How should a Media3 app pause for phone calls? Ours keeps playing.

input.query: Media3 audio focus pause phone calls

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}, {"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "behind-live-window", "title": "BehindLiveWindowException in Media3 / ExoPlayer live streams", "text": "# BehindLiveWindowException in Media3 / ExoPlayer live streams

A live stream exposes a sliding window of segments. If playback falls further behind than
the window (long pause, slow network, app in the background), the segments it needs are gone
and the player raises a `BehindLiveWindowException`, surfaced as a `PlaybackException` with
error code `ERROR_CODE_BEHIND_LIVE_WINDOW`.

Fix: in `Player.Listener.onPlayerError`, check for that error code, then call
`player.seekToDefaultPosition()` followed by `player.prepare()` to rejoin at the live edge.
Consider a longer live window on the server or a smaller target live offset on the client."}]}

An MP4 file's index (the `moov` atom) is often written at the end of the file by recorders and
encoders. A progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can
begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests.

Checks and fix:
- `ffprobe -v trace file.mp4 2>&1 | grep -m2 -E "type:'(moov|mdat)'"` shows which atom comes first.
- Remux with the index at the front: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart out.mp4`.
- For adaptive streaming, prefer fragmented MP4 (DASH or HLS) instead."}, {"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel")`.
- A device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or a failed keybox
  provisioning; the license server then refuses HD keys.
- Log the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal apart from a
  network or provisioning error."}]}

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

Checks:
- Ask the display what it supports: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` (or `Display.isHdr()` on API 26+).
- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason
  HDR output gets flattened.
- Confirm the decoder output format reports the expected colour transfer
  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.
- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or
  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}, {"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}]}

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.
- Too many codec instances are alive at once. Hardware codecs are a shared, limited resource;
  release codecs you no longer use.

messages.content: [MD-4141] Our podcast app keeps playing during phone calls. How do we fix it?

input.query: audio focus pause phone calls

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}, {"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "behind-live-window", "title": "BehindLiveWindowException in Media3 / ExoPlayer live streams", "text": "# BehindLiveWindowException in Media3 / ExoPlayer live streams

A live stream exposes a sliding window of segments. If playback falls further behind than
the window (long pause, slow network, app in the background), the segments it needs are gone
and the player raises a `BehindLiveWindowException`, surfaced as a `PlaybackException` with
error code `ERROR_CODE_BEHIND_LIVE_WINDOW`.

Fix: in `Player.Listener.onPlayerError`, check for that error code, then call
`player.seekToDefaultPosition()` followed by `player.prepare()` to rejoin at the live edge.
Consider a longer live window on the server or a smaller target live offset on the client."}]}

{"results": [{"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel")`.
- A device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or a failed keybox
  provisioning; the license server then refuses HD keys.
- Log the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal apart from a
  network or provisioning error."}]}

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}]}

Likely cause: Probably not a player bug: the file itself has a stream offset. ffprobe reports the video stream start_time at 0.300000 and the audio at 0.000000, so video begins 300 ms after audio, which matches voices being heard before the lips move.

messages.content: [MD-4182] hdr10_hevc_1080p.mp4 shows a black screen or washed-out colours on the lumen-l3. Why?

input.query: HDR10 HEVC Main10 display HDR support

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

Checks:
- Ask the display what it supports: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` (or `Display.isHdr()` on API 26+).
- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason
  HDR output gets flattened.
- Confirm the decoder output format reports the expected colour transfer
  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.
- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or
  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}, {"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}]}

content.text:
Likely cause: The clip is HEVC Main 10 (10-bit, BT.2020, PQ), but lumen-l3's only HEVC decoder (c2.lumen.hevc.decoder) supports the Main profile, so it cannot properly decode 10-bit content, which fits a black screen. Next step: Serve lumen-l3 an 8-bit SDR rendition (H.264 or HEVC Main), or tone-map to SDR, and only select HDR10 renditions when a Main10 decoder and an HDR display are reported.

content.text:
Likely cause: The thumbnail grid opens more simultaneous hardware AVC decoders than the lumen-l3 allows. The device supports at most 4 concurrent hardware video decoders, and the log shows five `c2.lumen.avc.decoder` allocations followed by "Failed to create component ... (NO_MEMORY: max instances reached)" and a `CodecException` in ThumbGrid at position=4, so the instance limit is the cause, not the stream format.
Next step: Cap concurrent decoders at 4 or fewer, ideally 1-2 (share or queue a small pool), and call `release()` on each thumbnail codec as soon as its frame is extracted, so later items can allocate one. Alternatively, use `MediaMetadataRetriever` for the frames.
